key_insight: AlphaTensor-Quantum can be reused and extended without retraining to optimize a wide range of quantum circuits, delivering larger reductions in T-count than previous circuit-specific methods while remaining generalizable and efficient.
problem_solved: High T-counts in fault-tolerant quantum circuits drive resource costs and limit practical quantum algorithm execution; existing optimizers often need retraining or are specialized to particular circuit families.
method: Reuse the pre-trained AlphaTensor-Quantum model as a general optimizer rather than retraining for each new circuit family.
Extend the model’s search and transformation capabilities to target T-count directly across diverse circuit topologies and synthesis patterns.
Apply a cost-driven optimization loop that evaluates candidate rewrites/syntheses for T-count reduction while preserving circuit semantics.
impact: Cuts resource overheads for fault-tolerant quantum programs, making larger and more complex quantum algorithms more feasible for researchers and engineers without repeated model training.
visual_elements: Before/after bar chart showing T-count reductions across representative circuits (e.g., arithmetic, quantum chemistry, oracles).
Pipeline diagram illustrating reuse: pre-trained AlphaTensor-Quantum → optimization loop → diverse circuits (no retraining).
Heatmap or scatter plot mapping circuit types to percent T-count reduction to show generalizability.
Icon set: stopwatch (efficiency), chip (hardware), wrench (optimization), and stacked gates (T-count)
paper_title: Reusability report: Optimizing T count in general quantum circuits with AlphaTensor-Quantum
paper_authors: Remmy Zen, Maximilian Nägele, Florian Marquardt
